author: TEDx Talks
description:
We have all heard the story that most lottery winners end up broke. The truth, however, is  that it’s a myth. But the problem it points to, Sudden Wealth Syndrome, is very real. From college athletes signing their first NIL deal, to young professionals receiving a bonus, to families navigating an inheritance, sudden money creates emotional whiplash that can turn excitement into fear, guilt, and regret. In his talk, Tom Henske unpacks why smart people make “Ready, Fire, Aim” mistakes when money arrives. He shares the 4 P’s that transform sudden wealth from chaos into clarity. 

Tom Henske, a two-time All-American and three-time NCAA National Champion at the University of Virginia, carried that high-pressure discipline into the world of personal finance. With nearly 30 years as a Certified Financial Planner, he founded his own firm, guided it through a public acquisition, and earned credentials including CFP®, ChFC®, and SE-AWMA®. He is the author of NIL Financial Playbook, It Makes Tot
title: Why suddenly having money (often) goes wrong | Tom Henske | TEDxNaples

author: TEDx Talks
description: This TEDx talk explores the fragile relationship between humans and wildlife through a deeply personal story from rural Tanzania, where nightly encounters with elephants can mean fear, loss, and even death. This talk aims to reframe human–elephant conflict not as a battle to be won, but as a communication problem to be solved. It highlights an unexpected solution, beehive fences, inspired by research from conservation biologist Lucy King, to show how designing with nature, rather than against it, can protect communities while allowing wildlife to thrive. Ultimately, the talk argues that the future of conservation depends not on force, but on understanding, creativity, and coexistence. Sydney Becker is an undergraduate student at Scripps College studying biology and psychology, whose primary interests are caring for animals and the world they inhabit. Sydney’s experiences range from hands-on work with animals in both captive and wild settings to fieldwork in Tanzania, where she assiste
title: How bees could help save elephants | Sydney Lynn Becker | TEDxClaremont Graduate University

author: TEDx Talks
description: Noah Levin's talk invites us to reconsider the systems that put our food on the table. He highlights how the food sovereignty framework could serve as a more equitable and sustainable system. Noah is a Brazilian-American senior at Haverford College passionate about federal policy and food system reform. His passion for food policy extends into other work, interning with Senator Cory Booker, working on a local county’s food policy council, and creating and teaching a for-credit Haverford course on global food systems. Post-graduation, Noah hopes to work on the Hill as a federal policymaker. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Confronting the Other: Violence, Desire, Fantasies of Freedom | Noah Levin | TEDxHaverford College

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Clifford explores the connections we make through the 'festa', whether a community can define our individual identity, and how humans collectively evolve their sense of belonging to create experiences larger than ourselves. With a strong academic background in Maltese and European history and Baroque studies, and currently pursuing a PhD in cultural tourism, Clifford brings a deep understanding of heritage and identity. His career spans media, where he has worked as a presenter, producer, and TV director, alongside his work as a self-published author.
Since 2024, he has served as Malta’s High Commissioner to Namibia, while also acting as President of the Northern Region, driving initiatives across environmental, cultural, and educational sectors.
A member of the Young Elected Politicians programme, Clifford has contributed to EU policymaking and represented the programme at COP27 and COP29. He has also addressed the United Nations High-Level Political Forum on Sustainable Development
title: How local village feasts can still bring us together | Clifford Galea Vella | TEDxUniversityofMalta

author: TEDx Talks
description: Bela's talk examines the violent and expansive possibilities of contact with another person as central to the (re-)constitution of the self. Bela Khanna (she/her) graduated from Haverford in 2024 with a double major in Philosophy and English with Creative Writing. Bela is headed to Villanova this fall to pursue a doctoral degree in Philosophy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Confronting the other: Violence, desire, fantasies of freedom | Bela Khanna | TEDxHaverford College

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Crystal Yu has tried a lot of activities. She's walked away from most of them. But she has been figure skating for six years through early mornings, long weekends, and days where nothing went right and has never once quit. In this talk, Crystal explores what made that one thing different from all the others, and why most people confuse being impressive with being fulfilled.
 Crystal is a 13-year-old student in Collingwood School, West Vancouver. She has been figure skating for six years and has competed internationally. She enjoys ballet, reading, snowboarding and walking her maltipoo, Miu Miu. Crystal is also a member of the Junior CBO (Collingwood Business Organization). This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Your passion isn't your talent, it's what you can't quit | Crystal Yu | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the key to deeper connection isn’t what you say—but what you smell? Aroma has the extraordinary ability to unlock memory, bridge cultures, and transform ordinary moments into unforgettable experiences. Jeremy Storton reveals how awakening your sense of smell can change the way you connect with people, places, and yourself. Jeremy Storton’s journey into the world of beer began with simple curiosity and a homebrewing hobby in 2007. What started as an interest quickly evolved into a deep exploration of flavor, aroma, and sensory experience, eventually leading him to become one of only a few hundred Advanced Cicerones worldwide and a respected global beer educator.
After tasting thousands of beers across more than a hundred styles, Jeremy became fascinated by a broader realization: humans are far more capable tasters than most people believe. His work now focuses on the connection between aroma, perception, and human potential, exploring how our senses shape the way we experience
title: The Superpower Right Under Your Nose | Jeremy Storton | TEDxBend

author: TEDx Talks
description: Creative operations leader Ryan Garney opened his TEDxBeverlyGrove 2026 talk with the story of two nearly identical ocean liners, the Olympic and the Titanic, one that survived a collision and one that sank. What followed was not a history lesson. It was a personal account of losing his father while running a high pressure job, and the collapse from never processing the grief. Drawing on neuroscience and his breakdown, Garney closes with the line that gives the talk its title: three mental bulkheads that keep the ship from sinking. Ryan Garney is a creative operations leader who has spent over a decade managing teams through high-pressure production environments in entertainment and media. A Triple Crown Award Recipient from Toastmasters International, he has competed in the World Championship of Public Speaking and served as Immediate Past President of the West Hollywood Toastmasters Chapter, leading the club to President's Distinguished status and recognition as one of the top clubs
title: Mental Bulkheads: Why the Olympic Survived and the Titanic Didn't | Ryan Garney | TEDxBeverly Grove

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Experience the power of live music through an expressive saxophone performance of “Have Your Way,” an original composition by Joshua Nathaniel Bennett. The performance brings melody, emotion, and artistry together in a captivating musical moment. Joshua Nathaniel Bennett is a Birmingham, Alabama native. After taking piano lessons at Birmingham Southern, he developed a deep love for the art that continued to grow as he mastered the saxophone in middle and high school. Joshua earned top ratings in solo and ensemble competitions and performed with distinguished honor bands including All County, the UAB Honor Band, the UAB Jazz Summit, and the Samford Honor Band.

Joshua played with the UAB Big Band under the direction of Dr. Steven Roberts during the induction of jazz legend Harry Belafonte into the Alabama Jazz Hall of Fame. He later founded the band Soul Collaboration, opening for internationally acclaimed smooth jazz artist Eric Essix and performing at major community events such as J
title: Music Performance  | Joshua Bennett | TEDxAlabaster

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Movement becomes a powerful expression of emotion in this captivating dance performance. Eryn Cade performs to “Prayer,” an original composition by Jasmine Garfield, bringing music and movement together in a compelling artistic interpretation Eryn is an interdisciplinary dance artist and research-based choreographer whose work speaks where words cannot. An Assistant Professor of Dance at Alabama State University, she holds a BFA and MFA in Dance from the University of Alabama, where her research on the Black female body and the colonial gaze earned an Artistic Achievement Award. She is a finalist for the Young Choreographers Festival, with work presented at the Joyce Theater in New York City.

Her performance career spans concert and commercial stages, including international work in Toulouse, France, and appearances at the 2022 World Games alongside artists such as Tony! Toni! Toné!, Bootsy Collins, and Sheila E. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but
title: Dance Performance  | Eryn Cade | TEDxAlabaster

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Fear. Every competitor knows the feeling that shows up right before a match begins. Five years into competitive Taekwondo, Sunny learned what to do with it. It changed how he performs on the mat, on stage, and in any circumstance where something is at stake.

 Sunny is an 11-year-old who holds a second-degree Taekwondo black belt. He has competed in national martial arts championships to Chinese poetry recitation on a world stage. He MCs professional events, sings and performs hip-hop. Sunny plays soccer and basketball and spends time with his British Shorthair cat. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Don't fight fear, listen to what it's telling you | Sunny Jiang | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Most kids are told to figure out who they are. But that only happens through trying, failing, and trying again. In this talk, Cynthia shares the moments she was completely certain about herself, and completely mistaken, and what those moments taught her about self-discovery, friendship, and why staying curious about yourself might matter more than having all the answers.
 Cynthia is a friendly 9-year-old student who enjoys reading and is always exploring new interests. She also trains in gymnastics, and is an avid piano player who has performed in front of audiences. She has a natural aptitude for drawing and loves to illustrate cats. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Self-discovery: Getting It wrong Is how you get It right  | Cynthia Qiu | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We spend most of our lives waiting — for the weekend, the result, the moment worth posting — while the ordinary days quietly slip past unnoticed. Yimin makes a case for the everyday moments: the unremarkable Tuesdays, the unscripted evenings, the experiences we treat as filler between the highlights. He argues that the life we keep waiting to start is already happening, and that learning to notice it, and relish it, is the most important thing any of us can practice right now.
 Yimin is a 15-year-old student who is an accomplished musician playing both piano and violin. A committed multi-sport athlete, he plays competitive basketball as a point guard and is also a certified referee, scorekeeper, and coach. He also serves as the Vancouver District Representative on the student council. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What we're missing while we wait for life to get exciting | Yimin Yang | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We teach kids that love is a feeling. Elizabeth, who lost her dog at eight years old, discovered something different. When a new puppy came home, she took on feeding, walking, and training her every single day. What she found is that love isn't an emotion, it's a practice, built with routine, patience, and showing up even when you're tired. 
This is a talk about love, responsibility, and what kids are actually capable of when you give them something to take care of. Elizabeth is a 9-year-old Grade 3 student in White Rock, BC. She enjoys a wide range of sports such as basketball, swimming, soccer and horseback riding. Outside of sports, she plays the piano, and is active in arts, writing and public speaking. At home, she cares for Suki, her toy poodle. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Love isn't just what you feel, it's what you do | Elizabeth Cheng | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

He has consistently demonstrated how to guide raw talent toward international recognition. His philosophy centers on the power of collaboration: bringing the right people together to achieve extraordinary results. author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world driven by endless scrolling and instant gratification, this talk explores how digital platforms exploit the brain's dopamine-driven reward system, drawing parallels with a famous neuroscience experiment. Through relatable stories, humor, and practical strategies using the PAUSE framework, the talk shows how anyone can regain focus, calmness, and meaningful happiness by choosing intentional living over algorithm-driven habits. Arti Dosanjh is a strategic technology leader with expertise in delivering complex insurance platforms and driving product excellence within the financial services domain. As Director of Delivery for the P&C North America Insurance Platform at Sapiens, she leads cross-functional teams to build scalable solutions that solve real business challenges, blending technical vision with operational rigor. Her work reflects a deep understanding of both the business value and human impact of modern technology delivery, shaped by years of experience navigating hi
title: Reclaim Your Mind | Arti Dosanjh | TEDxChennai Institute of Technology Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
E se a saúde mental não estivesse restrita ao domínio da mente, mas fosse um fenômeno que emerge do ser integral que somos: corpo-emoção-linguagem?

Existe uma conexão profunda entre corpo, emoções e linguagem. A forma como respiramos, nos movemos e ocupamos o espaço não apenas revela o que sentimos — pode também transformar a maneira como sentimos e ampliar nossas possibilidades de ação. Nesta talk, Marta Magnus nos convida a olhar para o corpo como uma fonte de inteligência e autoconhecimento e mostra como pequenas mudanças na nossa corporalidade podem abrir novas possibilidades diante das emoções e dos desafios da vida.

Quem sabe o cuidado com nossa saúde mental começa por escutar aquilo que o corpo já está dizendo? Marta Magnus é consultora generativa e coach ontológico, credenciada MCC (Master Certified Coach) e ACTC (Advanced Certification in Team Coaching) pela ICF (International Coaching Federation), com mais de 17 anos de experiência em desenvolvimento de líderes e equipes.
title: A inteligência escondida no corpo | Marta Magnus | TEDxPorto Alegre Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Karunyaphat (Ryu) shares how discipline and hard work helped him make important changes in his life. He explains that he did not change all at once, but slowly built better habits through studying, sports, competitions, and daily effort. Along the way, he learned that motivation can disappear, while discipline helps us continue even when we do not feel motivated. His talk reminds us that big dreams require action, consistency, and the willingness to keep working toward the person we want to become.
 I am a member of the Year 8 class who is currently preparing to enter high school and future academic competitions. I deeply love Maths, Biology, Physics, and Astronomy. My hobbies are kickboxing, football, e-sports and studying. I am also interested in languages; besides English and Thai, I can speak some Chinese and am currently learning Japanese in my freetime. I am a very open-minded and a curious person who enjoys learning and gaining skills. And I have the two cutest dogs in the worl
title: The Equation of Effort | Karunyaphat Onnoi | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Nittaya takes a fun look at everyday school life and the lessons we learn from it. She talks about homework, group work, school rules, and other experiences that students know very well. Through these everyday challenges, she realizes that school teaches us more than academic subjects. School also teaches us how to think, adapt, and grow. Her talk reminds us that even the difficult and confusing parts of school can help prepare us for life.
 I’m a student from Grade 4 and I have a lot of fun learning at school. Sometimes lessons can be hard, but I try my best to get good grades. I am good at Math, but I love Art and Music most because of both the teacher and the subject itself. Sometimes, I get very surprised because on some days while on other days there is none, which I like and understand. For me, school is made for kids to learn, grow, and have fun. So, I want to keep my good grades up, and I think everyone else should too! This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED confere
title: What School Really Teaches Us | Nittaya Thamniyom | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Fae shares how being shy and afraid of the stage once kept her safely inside her comfort zone. When she was faced with situations she could not always avoid, she discovered that she could change the way she responded to fear instead of waiting for the fear to disappear. From her experience, she developed a simple three-step formula and through auditioning for a school play and eventually standing on the TEDx stage, Fae shows that courage does not mean becoming a different person. Courage means understanding yourself, accepting your fear, and choosing to move forward anyway.  I’m a Year 6 student who is not very talkative and loud, but I still have  big interests. At the moment, my biggest interests are life, animals, nature, drawing and psychology. Recently, I’ve discovered that I can sing and act. I want to try and grow by stepping more out of my comfort zone. My biggest dream in life is to be a successful psychologist. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference for
title: A Formula to Overcome Fear | Fae Kongkul | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Thammasat talks about how fear can begin with one small thought and quickly grow into many worries. She compares these thoughts to falling dominoes, where one “What if?” can lead to another and stop us from trying. When she decided to audition for a school play, she learned to face these worries instead of letting them control her choices. Her experience taught her that we do not always need confidence before we act - sometimes confidence comes after we take the first step. Hi, my name is Thammasat. I am 11 years old. I’m in Year 6. I love singing and drawing. My favorite subjects are Geography, Art, Music, and Computing. My dream is to become a singer, because I really like listening to music and singing, but I am really shy - even speaking in front of the class makes me nervous and scared, but I’ve been trying to overcome my stage fright  by becoming an actor on a school play, and that is what my talk is all about. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format
title: Stopping the Dominoes | Thammasat Srimai | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Aratchaporn talks about how she once disliked drawing because it made her feel frustrated and stressed. After joining Art Club, she was able to experience art in a more patient and supportive way. She realized that sometimes we think we dislike something because our first experience with it was difficult. Her story encourages us to give things another chance because a new experience may help us discover something we never knew we could enjoy. Hello. I’m Poon. I’m a 6th grader who is trying to learn new things. I’m interested in arts and music - mostly drawing. My passion is animation. All my interest in animation is not only fun, but it keeps me relaxed and happy. My talk is about my experience of disliking drawing before but then love it again. My hobbies are drawing and reading books. I love reading books because it’s fun and my drawing style is similar to Chibi style. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local communit
title: Learning to Love Something Again  | Aratchaporn Jitnupong | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Kanapos shares how he changed from a very shy student into someone who better understands himself and his responsibilities. Along the way, he had to deal with procrastination and learn how to manage his time and studies. By setting smaller goals, staying organized, and asking for help, he began to build better habits. His story shows that growing up is not about becoming perfect, but about understanding ourselves and making choices that help us become better. I am Knan. I’m a Year 8 student who likes to try new things. I like Math and Computing because it’s just fun in general. My hobbies are playing games and playing football with friends. I’ll dream that one day I will have a job that fits who I am. My talk is about how I discovered who I am from my school life and experiences. I wish my talk would be inspiring and make people realize the importance of school. Thanks! This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community
title: Becoming the Person You Need to Be | Kanapos Tantiyavut | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Poon asks why time can sometimes feel very slow and, at other times, seem to disappear. Through his experience with gaming and procrastination, he realized how easily distractions can take away time without us noticing. He began to understand that managing time starts with being aware of how we use it each day. His talk encourages us to think carefully about our choices and ask ourselves whether we are using our time in ways that help us grow.
 I’m Poon. I’m in 5th grade and I enjoy a lot of things, specifically playing any sort of games or just hanging out with friends. I like Science, Math, and PE, sometimes coding. I play sports, mainly football. Though I am not very athletic, I don’t struggle with most physical activities. I try to be friendly with everyone. My talk is going to be about time, how we experience it, and how I disappointed myself from being irresponsible. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local commun
title: Why Time Feels Different | Poonyapat Panrong | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Punnada shares how she kept trying for a main role in a school play even after facing disappointment several times. When she decided to audition one more time, she finally got the opportunity she had been hoping for. The experience taught her that confidence does not always come before we try; sometimes we become confident because we choose to try. Her story encourages us not to give up too quickly, because one more attempt may lead to an opportunity we never expected. I am Pangpun, a Year 5 student who enjoys music, singing, dancing and learning new things. I also like Math and English because they challenge me to keep improving. In my talk “Just One More Try”, I will share how one embarrassing moment on stage taught me an important lesson about confidence and courage. I hope my story can inspire others to stay positive, believe in themselves and never give up after making mistakes. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a l
title: Just Try One More Time | Punnada Numchaiwattana | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Worawiwat (Pokpong) explores what it really means to make something a priority. He explains that important goals are often pushed aside because we tell ourselves we will work on them when we have more time. Through his own experience with homework and deadlines, he learned that even a few focused minutes can lead to progress. His talk encourages us to make time for the things that matter instead of waiting for free time to appear.
 My name is Worawiwat Thayawiwat a.k.a Pokpong. I am deeply interested in technology, innovation, and global developments. I enjoy exploring fields such as artificial intelligence, medical technologies, and engineering - as I am passionate about creating ideas that can influence society in meaningful ways. Beyond my seriousness in academics, I have experienced making school projects mainly on engineering and coding and building apps. I also participate in  managing school events - being part of the student council, an MC for several events, leading the techn
title: Schedule Your Priorities | Worawiwat Thayawiwat | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Isabelle shares how her idea of motivation changed as she grew older. At first, rewards like ice cream and gold medals encouraged her to try difficult things, including math competitions. As she continued practicing, she began to enjoy seeing herself improve and became more confident in her abilities. Isabelle shows us that rewards can help us get started, but believing in ourselves can give us a stronger reason to keep going. Hi, my name is Isabelle, and I am 10 years old. I love arts and crafts, listening to music, playing tennis, and spending time with my family and friends. I also love traveling and visiting new places, and I feel lucky to have seen lots of different countries already. My favourite school subjects are P.E - because it is so much fun and I get to run around, Maths and English because the lessons are always fun. In my talk “The Golden Choice” I share how saying “YES” to a difficult challenge helped me become more confident and believe in myself. This talk was given
title: The Golden Choice | Isabelle Anu Bird | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Atikun (Henry) shares what he learned while building a LEGO football robot for a school project. At first, the project was much harder than he expected, and he even wondered if he was good at building things. By continuing one piece at a time, he discovered that difficult things often become easier when we keep practicing. His talk reminds us that when something feels hard, it does not always mean we should stop. It may mean that we are learning and growing.
 My name is Henry. I’m a 2nd grader. I’m interested in Science, Engineering, football, swimming and playing Lego. My talk is about “What Hard Really Means”. My dream is to become a pilot. I love airplanes and enjoy looking down from above. For me, it feels exciting, fun and challenging. I believe we can make it if we don’t give up. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What Hard Really Means | Atikun Scholand | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Atipatsada, or Bella as her family and friends would call her, shares her experience of being afraid to speak in front of other people. A school presentation gave her the chance to face this fear, even though she still felt nervous. With support from a friend and the courage to step onto the stage, she discovered that being brave does not mean having no fear. Her story shows that courage can begin with one small step, and that facing our fears can help us become stronger and more confident.
 I’m Bella, and I am 9 years old. My talk is about the first time I was on stage. So when I was a kid, my goal was to be the best daughter ever, like everyone. I love PE, arts and the clubs I joined. The sports that I do is tennis, but what I like to play is volleyball, football, and a little bit of badminton and basketball. But I don’t really play badminton. My goal right now is to be a model, doctor, or a tennis champion, and my favorite singer is almost all of them because they are all so good.
title: The Silence Before the Stage | Atipatsada Phophon | TEDxUnicorn British School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Avery's talk is adapted from her classics thesis, which is on disability representation in ancient literature. She looks forward to sharing how disability-informed readings of texts can open up new and liberatory interpretations Avery Barnett is a recent graduate of Haverford College, double majoring in classics and mathematics. In the fall, she will be moving to London to pursue a Master’s degree in Medieval and Renaissance intellectual history. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Reading against the lines: Disability representation | Avery Barnett | TEDxHaverford College

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this empowering talk, Jessica Maren dismantles one of the most invisible barriers to progress: the belief that we must be validated, endorsed, or chosen before we take action. Maren explores how our biological wiring inherently prioritizes social safety and approval over disruption, turning hesitation into an unconscious behavioral autopilot. By combining neurological insight with personal storytelling, this talk reframes waiting for permission as a learned pattern that can be broken—equipping audiences to understand the true friction of courage, choose alignment over external validation, and step forward into leadership without waiting for an invitation. Jessica Maren holds a Master’s in Teaching in Biological Sciences, and she has spent years speaking to entrepreneurs, leaders, and community groups. Jessica bridges scientific literacy with practical application, translating complex biological principles into real possibilities for change. Through workshops and keynote-style talks
title: Permission Is a Pattern | Jessica Maren | TEDxU Chicago Illinois

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this deeply moving talk, Yasin Arfat explores the transformative power of resilience and what it means to rise above circumstances that seem impossible to overcome. Drawing from lived experiences as a refugee, a member of a marginalized community, and a genocide survivor, Arfat reflects on navigating displacement, educational barriers, and profound uncertainty. Through unwavering perseverance, community support, and advocacy for human rights, this talk reveals that our hardships do not define our potential—demonstrating how resilience is not merely about survival, but a powerful catalyst for leadership, purpose, and lasting change. Yasin Arfat is a prominent refugee advocate, and his work is rooted in lived experience and a commitment to uplifting displaced communities. As a former refugee himself, he leads organizational strategy, coordinates field operations, and works directly with refugee camps in Bangladesh to ensure access to resources. Yasin is committed to amplifying the vo
title: From Genocide to Hope: The Rohingya Journey | Yasin Arfat | TEDxU Chicago Illinois
